mechanism: Rivastigmine (cholinesterase inhibitor) enhances acetylcholine effects while oxybutynin (anticholinergic) antagonizes them, creating direct pharmacodynamic opposition and increased risk of cholinergic toxicity or reduced efficacy of both agents.
action: Avoid concurrent use if possible; if combination necessary, monitor closely for cholinergic symptoms (salivation, bronchospasm, bradycardia) and anticholinergic symptoms (dry mouth, urinary retention), and consider alternative agents with less direct opposition.
